TEST TEST TEST

I am broadly interested in how and why organisms respond to their environment. My long-term career goal is to lead a research lab integrating physiological ecology with developmental psychobiology to untangle the proximate mechanisms and ultimate implications of plasticity across development. I work under a [developmental systems framework](https://deltacenter.uiowa.edu/developmental-systems), which means I approach development as a life-long process resulting from complex interactions between genes, tissue, social environment, broader climate, and more. My undergraduate research projects utilized techniques in behavior and neuroscience to examine how motor-related gene knockout affected development of mouse grooming behavior and sensorimotor cortex over five early ages. My graduate work joins physiological ecology with my advisor’s expertise in social behavior to examine the developmental and activational impact of increasing temperature on parenting behavior and its development, using methods in neuroethology and transcriptomics to investigate developmental drivers of social behavior and provide insight into the complex and multidirectional ways environments and individuals interact.

Research topics of interest:

thermoregulation, neuroendocrinology, animal behavior, physiological ecology, developmental psychobiology
